financial_property_loss: Rs. 28.49 crores loss to State Bank of Patiala
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the argument that quashing criminal proceedings on the basis of a settlement between the complainant and the accused would encroach upon the jurisdiction of the other organs of government and violate the rule of law.

legal_representation.accused: Bishwajit Bhattacharya, Sr. Adv., Daya Krishan Sharma, Rohit Vats, Ms. Monika Sharma, Advs.
legal_representation.state: Ms. Pinky Anand, ASG., Rajiv Nanda, B. V. Balramdas, Rajesh Ranjan, Ms. Kritika Sachdeva, M. K. Maroria, Arvind Kumar Sharma, Advs.

investigation_status: FIR registered on 28.12.2001, charge-sheet filed, trial completed

appeal_history.trial_court: Dismissed application for compounding of offences
appeal_history.high_court: Quashed FIR and consequential proceedings on basis of settlement

prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the High Court's quashing of the FIR and consequential proceedings on the basis of a settlement between the complainant and the accused was an encroachment on the judiciary's role and a violation of the rule of law, which is a basic structure of the Constitution.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the High Court had judiciously considered the facts and circumstances of the case, and that the offences in the present case were not heinous, thus justifying the quashing of the criminal proceedings based on the settlement.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the doctrine of judicial restraint, emphasizing that the judiciary should not encroach upon the domain of the legislative or executive branches and should not direct compounding of non-compoundable offences.
precedent_relied_upon: Manoj Sharma v. State & Ors. (2008) 16 SCC 1; State of Tamil Nadu v. R. Vasanthi Stanley & Anr. (2016) 1 SCC 376; Central Bureau of Investigation v. A. Ravishankar Prasad & Ors. (2009) 6 SCC 351; Central Bureau of Investigation v. Maninder Singh (2016) 1 SCC 389; Gian Singh v. State of Punjab & Anr. (2012) 10 SCC 303; Kulwinder Singh & Ors. v. State of Punjab & Anr. (2007) (4) CTC 769; Mrs. Shakuntala Sawhney v. Mrs. Kaushalya Sawhney & Ors. (1980) 1 SCC 63
